evidence: The export holds this man twice: as an undated stub who is Salvatore Mazza's father (@I22@, component 1), and as "Rosario Mazza b. 1850 of Piedimonte Etneo" married to a Leonarda with no surname, heading the 110-person component 2 (@I23@). FIVE independent records make them one man. (1) Nati 1873 atto 3: Salvatore Mazza born 5 Jan 1873 to ROSARIO MAZZA DI MARIANO, 28, and LEONARDA BONANNO. (2) Marriage proclamation 1898: Mazza Salvatore, 25, son of Rosario, 53, and Bonanno Leonarda. (3) Marriage proclamation 1902: Mazza GIOVANNI, 27, son of Rosario, 55, and Bonanno Leonarda. (4) Marriage proclamation 1910: Mazza IGNAZIO, 23, son of Rosario, 65, and Bonanno Leonarda, both parents present and consenting. (5) Nati 1877 atto 168: ORAZIO Mazza born to Rosario, 31, and Leonarda. The tree's @I23@ has exactly these sons - Orazio, Ignazio, Giovanni - by a wife called Leonarda. Rosario's ages give a birth about 1845; the tree says 1850.

THE EXPORT HOLDS THIS MAN TWICE, one letter apart: «Guiseppi Polistena» born 1874 at Scilla (@I130@) and «Giuseppi Polistena» born 1875 at Scilla (@I139@). The evidence is inside the export and the automatic rules missed it only because the given names differ by a letter. BOTH ARE MARRIED TO THE SAME WOMAN, Giuseppa D'Ascoli, and BOTH ARE THE FATHER OF THE SAME CHILD, Joseph A Polistena — which is this archive's own standard for a merge, identical spouse AND identical child. The kept copy carries the parents (Antonio Polistena and Giovanna Pontillo) and six children; the dropped one carries a wife and one child, all of which the kept copy already has. Born 1874 against 1875 is the ordinary one-year drift.

THE EXPORT HOLDS THIS WOMAN TWICE, born at BUENOS AIRES in 1930 (@I202@) and 1933 (@I194@). Again the evidence is internal.
